title: When Clinical Judgment Becomes a Predictive Shortcut: Two Questions Clinical AI Must Answer Before Deployment
abstract: arXiv:2609.25852v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Clinical AI can predict outcomes using information generated by existing clinical judgment. Such performance alone cannot establish usefulness before recognition or across care processes. We propose evidence requirements matched to intended use and information conditions, with additional state-reference and proxy-relative timing tests for stronger recognition claims. This framework helps hospitals assess whether the conditions supporting performance hold when assistance is most needed. These questions remain outside current evaluation practice leakage checks, overall predictive performance, and external validation do not address them; the framework makes them explicit and specifies the direct evidence required to answer them.

translated_title: 当临床判断成为预测捷径：临床AI部署前必须回答的两个问题
translated_abstract: 临床人工智能可以利用现有临床判断所产生的信息来预测结果，但仅凭这样的性能无法证明其在识别诊断之前或整个诊疗过程中的有用性。我们提出了与预期用途和信息条件相匹配的证据要求，并针对更强的识别声明额外增加了状态参照测试和代理相对时序测试。该框架帮助医院评估在最需要辅助的时刻，支持模型性能的条件是否仍然成立。这些问题在当前的评估实践中仍未被涉及——数据泄露检查、整体预测性能和外部验证都无法回答它们；该框架使这些问题明确化，并规定了回答这些问题所需的直接证据。
tldr: 该论文提出一个与预期用途相匹配的证据要求框架，指出临床AI利用临床判断信息的预测性能本身不足以证明其有用性，并通过状态参照与代理相对时序两项测试，帮助医院在部署前验证模型在最需要辅助时性能条件是否仍然成立。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an evidence requirements framework arguing that clinical AI's predictive performance alone cannot establish usefulness, and introduces state-reference and proxy-relative timing tests to help hospitals verify whether performance conditions hold when assistance is most needed before deployment.
